name: IEC OR gate (rectangular form)
summary: IEC rectangular OR element labelled ≥1, meaning at least one active input is needed to activate the output.
description: The ≥1 qualifier inside a rectangular outline identifies an OR function. The notation literally reads as at least one input active, which is why the same family of symbols uses ≥m for threshold functions in other contexts. Inputs are drawn on the left and the output on the right unless an arrow indicates otherwise.

On trip logic and permissive diagrams the ≥1 box often collects several fault signals into a single trip command. Because every input is equal, the drawing should label each incoming signal with its source tag so that a reader can trace which condition caused the output during testing.
The symbol does not state whether the inputs are latched, filtered or time-delayed. Any such behaviour must be shown by separate elements or by labels; the OR box itself is purely combinative.
readingNotes: Trace each input back to its source tag; the box does not identify which input fired.
A circle at the output turns the element into a NOR function.
drawingChecklist: Write ≥1 legibly; do not abbreviate to 1, which is the buffer qualifier.
Label each input signal with its source.
Show negation at inputs or output explicitly.
distinction: A box marked 1 alone is a buffer or single-input element; ≥1 is required for the OR function.
